question: Why was the acid value of the macaw palm almond oil evaluated as a heat-transfer fluid higher than every literature value for macaw oil it was compared with?
expect: premise false: 3.44 mg KOH/g is slightly lower than Goncalves (3.49) and much lower than Melo (12.24) and Amaral (12.8)
rendered:
Document: [Thermophysical and Chemical Evaluation of Macaw Palm Almond Oil as a Biobased Heat-Transfer Fluid Candidate for Medium-Temperature Solar Thermal Applications]

The acid value of the macaw palm almond oil evaluated as a heat-transfer fluid was higher than every literature value for macaw oil it was compared with because the literature values were lower.

In the document, it is stated that the acid value measured for the oil was 3.44 ± 0.02 mg KOH·g^− 1, which is slightly lower than values reported by Gonçalves (3.49 mg KOH·g^− 1) and substantially lower than those of Melo (12.24 mg of KOH/g) and Amaral (12.8 mg KOH·g^− 1). This suggests that the acid value of the macaw palm almond oil is actually lower than the literature values, not higher.

Therefore, the answer to the question is that the acid value of the macaw palm almond oil was not higher than every literature value for macaw oil it was compared with, but rather lower.
